reviews.review:
I'm going to throw my hat into the ring regarding the review bombing and every other review bombing that is likely to come after.
Helldivers 2 is [i]still[/i] a very good, visually stunning game that will provide you a unique experience with incredible value for money. The trouble with it is that the devs have consistent bad habits: they keep repeating the mistakes they say they're moving past, like making negative balance changes on a whim, releasing content with bugs (not the kind you shoot at), missing some patch notes, and breaking older content for a while before it gets fixed. A lot of players consider this disrespect and/or incompetence, enough to elicit literal hatred for the devs by players and content creators alike. If you're not prepared to deal with that, then yeah, don't play this game. Otherwise, I urge you to just play it for yourself and form your own opinion instead of falling for waves of sensationalism that the Internet loves to push.

[h2]Original Review[/h2]
There are two big things which make this game a modern classic that dwarfs every AAA release since the turn of the decade.

[h2]1. Absolute Cinema[/h2]
Every casual moment of this game looks like the final battle of a sci-fi movie. The giant explosion particles which would make the US Army blush; the voices of Helldivers laughing with glee as they mag dump LMGs into tidal waves of bugs; the sight of enemies the size of a large house slowly lumbering towards you as your squad scrambles to prepare anti-tank weapons. Frankly, more games should use the art direction of "everything is a cinematic" - it's just too obvious.

[h2]2. The Biggest LARP in Gaming History[/h2]
What makes Helldivers truly special is the meta-narrative with which the entire game is conjoined. Everything that you do influences a larger, real-time Galactic War with real, changing frontlines, capturable planets which become invaded, death tolls ranging in the millions per planet, and limited-time events with real, permanent consequences for victory and defeat. Letting hundreds of thousands of people work together to uphold Managed Democracy and influence the future of official lore creates a powerful sense of unity the likes of which nothing has captured since vanilla World of Warcraft.
It's a good game at a fair price with developers that actually care. Sure, Sony/PS sucks, but I guess you can't have everything.
